en.title: Minimum Rooks Left When Rooks Can Only Capture
en.description:
On the board, 1 is a rook and 0 is an empty cell. A rook can only move along its row or column to capture another rook it meets; it cannot jump over other rooks and cannot move to an empty cell. Keep capturing, and find the minimum number of rooks left once no two of them attack each other.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, editorial and tests; missing original bounds and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the statement.
en.input: The first line contains the number of rows n and the number of columns m, followed by n lines of m values, each 0 or 1. The original bounds are 1≤n,m≤1000, and a completely empty board is allowed.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are 1; 3; and 0, checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Treat rows and columns as the vertices of a bipartite graph, with each rook as an edge joining its row and its column. Merge all occupied positions with a union-find and count the connected components that contain edges.
